Name: RenataVasquezPham
Deal: She sells other crawlers things that are not hers, and the paperwork always holds up.
Story: Twenty-two years moving property nobody needed at prices nobody questioned. The Collapse changed her inventory and nothing else. She has sold the same safe room to three separate parties and been paid by all three. The System adores her, because contracts are its native language and she speaks it without an accent - it has quietly begun honouring her deeds as though she had the authority to write them. Nobody has established yet whether that means she does, or whether the System is simply enjoying the bit.
MechanicalHook: Vendor selling map access, safe-room rights and 'cleared' passage. Some of it is real. Working out which is a Charisma contest, not a hidden roll.

Name: OtisLange
Deal: He is still driving the route, and the route now goes down.
Story: Thirty-one years up and down Colfax. He came down in uniform and has not taken it off. Somewhere on Floor 2 he found something with wheels and started running a schedule, and he keeps it: he picks up, he does not exceed the limit, he does not deviate, and he does not stop for anything trying to kill you. He is not brave. He is on the clock, and the clock is the last piece of the old world still working.
MechanicalHook: A moving safe zone on a fixed timetable. Miss the stop and wait for the next one. Never fights, cannot be hurried, will not be argued with.

Name: BrickHalloran
Deal: The most sponsored crawler on the floor is a genuinely kind man being fattened for a ratings beat.
Story: Two seasons carrying a blocking sled for a team that never played him, beloved by exactly one bar in Englewood. The System found him in week one and gave him everything - gear drops, soft spawns, a highlight package with music over it. He shares the gear. He calls out traps for strangers. He has no idea he is a story arc, and arcs end. Killing him yourself would pay an obscene amount of Favor and would be the single most hated thing this party could do.
MechanicalHook: Joinable ally who buffs the party and is scheduled to die. The schedule may be breakable. The moral trap is the content.

Name: YukiOrdonezFrame
Deal: She eats the dungeon, and the dungeon has started eating back.
Story: Forty-eight tacos, regional record, laminated certificate behind the register. On Floor 1 she worked out that consuming monster parts lends you their traits for a while. She is four floors down now, formidable, and no longer entirely the shape she arrived in. She is warm, chatty and completely without malice. She would like to know what your party tastes like. Purely professionally.
MechanicalHook: Rival who is stronger every time you meet her, always wearing an ability the party has already seen on something they killed.

Name: TheSommelier
Deal: He finds a monster's weakness by tasting its blood, and he will not shut up about the finish.
Story: Twenty years on the floor of a restaurant that has not existed for some time. He refuses to give his name to anyone, on the grounds that a name is a liability inside a broadcast product - which is the most genre-aware sentence anyone in Denver has said out loud. He is right. The System cannot reference him in an announcement, cannot sponsor him and cannot build him into a story. His Favor is catastrophic and he considers this the point.
MechanicalHook: Sells real boss resistances. His namelessness is a live mechanic: announcements skip him, which is a genuine tactical advantage the party can borrow.

Name: DoloresOkonkwoReyes
Deal: She follows parties at a polite distance and prices what they leave behind.
Story: Thirty years of walking into houses after somebody died and putting a number on what was left. The job did not change. She never starts anything, is unfailingly courteous, and is always about eleven metres behind you. If you clear a room she prices the room. If you die in it she prices you, respectfully, and the audience finds this unbearably funny.
MechanicalHook: Non-hostile loot competitor. Can be raced, negotiated with or robbed - and robbing her costs Favor, because she is far more popular than the party.
Sponsor: Estate Solutions of the Front Range

Name: AugustinePell
Deal: They are citing the dungeon for safety violations, and the citations are landing.
Story: Career federal inspector, with a clipboard that survived the Collapse for reasons nobody can explain. They have filed 611 violations against Dungeon Crawler World: Earth - inadequate egress, unguarded machinery, no fall protection on the Falls. The System is obliged to log every one. It has started, very quietly, fixing some of them, and a fixed hazard is a hazard your party no longer has to survive.
MechanicalHook: Reporting a hazard to them permanently disables that trap for everyone. The System resents this and adjusts the difficulty somewhere the party is not looking.
Sponsor: (offer pending - they have not signed the release)

Name: MarisolTrejoAdeyemi
Deal: She will save anyone, including the thing that just tried to kill you.
Story: Eleven years in a trauma bay where you do not get to pick. She has not adjusted that policy and does not intend to. She has stabilised crawlers, stabilised a Debt Eater, and once spent an hour working on a Survey Drone before establishing it had never been alive. Parties love her right up until the first time she saves someone they wanted dead.
MechanicalHook: Healer who will absolutely revive an enemy in front of you. Recruitable, at the price of never getting to choose who lives.

Name: SisterAgnethaRoule
Deal: She keeps performing last rites, and it is corrupting the death metrics.
Story: Forty years of sitting with people at the end, and she does the identical job here. The problem is upstream: a death with a witness who calls it sacred does not convert cleanly into whatever the show is actually harvesting, and somebody several layers above the System AI has begun to notice a shortfall in the Denver numbers.
MechanicalHook: Meeting her enters the party in a ledger they cannot see. She will bless a body for free, and the party's next death behaves differently.

Name: CormacBui
Deal: He towed wrecks off the freeway for twenty years and now tows things that are still moving.
Story: Found a rig on the gridlock floor and put it straight back to work. He will haul your dead vehicle, your unconscious friend, or a monster you would rather fight somewhere with better footing. He invoices for all three. The invoices are real, itemised, and the System enforces them with enthusiasm.
MechanicalHook: Vehicle recovery, plus the tactical option of dragging a boss into terrain that suits you. Unpaid invoices become a debt encounter later.

Name: NadiaFerreiraStokes
Deal: She repairs armour with a dent puller and absolutely no ceremony.
Story: Built a business on Colorado's only real natural predator, the summer hailstorm, and she has never once been impressed by damage. She will fix your breastplate in four minutes, tell you what you did wrong to earn the dent, and quote you for the paint separately. She considers the monsters a supply-side problem.
MechanicalHook: Field repair. Restores durability cheaply and identifies what kind of attack made each mark - free intel on what is hunting the party.

Name: TerranceVoBell
Deal: He knows exactly where every sound in the amphitheatre goes, and so should you.
Story: Six summers mixing front-of-house on the best natural stage on the continent. He came down with in-ear monitors still around his neck and has been mapping the acoustics of every arena since. He can tell you where a boss cannot hear you, which is a thing bosses do not know about themselves. He is having, by some distance, the best time of anyone in this document.
MechanicalHook: Marks acoustic dead zones in arena fights - real stealth geometry on a floor that otherwise has none.

Name: HollyDrescherKaur
Deal: She survived the dive nobody survives, and management considers this a scheduling problem.
Story: Nineteen when she started diving into a chlorinated pool for tourists eating bad enchiladas, twenty-three when the venue was repossessed with the staff still inside. She is the only diver who came back up. The Cantina's new management has her listed for tonight's show, and every night's show, in perpetuity, and the listing is the thing keeping her there.
MechanicalHook: Floor 1 rescue. Freeing her means voiding a staff contract - a puzzle, not a fight. She joins as a mobility specialist who reaches places the party cannot.

Name: EliasWinterhalder
Deal: He is still doing the forecast, and down here the forecast is accurate.
Story: Four decades of pointing at a green wall and being wrong about Saturday with tremendous warmth. Underground, with no weather left to get wrong, he has quietly become the most reliable information source in Denver: he tracks hazard cycles, spawn timings and pressure changes, and delivers them in the exact cadence of a man telling you to take a jacket.
MechanicalHook: Gives real timing windows for environmental hazards. The forecast is genuinely correct, which the party will not believe until it saves them.

Name: PriyaBenavidezOkafor
Deal: She is documenting everything the dungeon does, for a trial that cannot happen.
Story: Bagged and tagged for nine years and cannot stop. She photographs kill sites, logs serial numbers on System-issued gear, and maintains a chain of custody on evidence for a prosecution with no court, no jurisdiction and no defendant that can be served. The System finds this hilarious. It has started leaving things out for her.
MechanicalHook: Trades from her archive. Her logs are the party's only route to knowing what the show did to a previous party in the room they are standing in.

Name: RubenAstorgaMbeki
Deal: He was foreclosing on people before the Syndicate made it a format, and he wants credit for it.
Story: Ran four buildings badly and profitably for twenty years, and arrived here genuinely excited - he recognised the business model immediately and assumed there would be a job in it. There was not. The System does not need middle management. He has spent three floors trying to get a meeting and has begun, slowly, to work out which side of the transaction he is on.
MechanicalHook: Comic antagonist who becomes a tragedy on a delay. Sells information he does not realise is worthless, and later, information he does not realise is priceless.

Name: JuneAbernathyCruz
Deal: They can talk to the things that were never given a voice module.
Story: Interpreted for city council, hospitals and one very long murder trial. Down here they worked out that several monster types signal intent with their bodies in a way that is consistent, learnable, and completely ignored by everyone busy screaming. They have now held four conversations with things the party has only ever fought.
MechanicalHook: Unlocks a non-combat resolution with at least one enemy family. The System does not offer this option and is visibly annoyed that it exists.
Sponsor: (under review - 'accessibility' is a difficult sell to the audience)

Name: TheQuietFloor
Deal: Somebody is clearing rooms ahead of the party and leaving nothing behind to show for it.
Story: Four separate parties have walked into an encounter already finished. No bodies, no loot, no damage to the room, and no announcement - and the last one is what frightens people, because the System announces everything. The prevailing theory in the bar is that they are very good. The less popular theory is that they are not a crawler.
MechanicalHook: Long-running mystery seed. Can stay unresolved for floors. Pays off whenever it is useful and costs nothing until then.

Name: AugustKesslerBoone
Deal: He is buying other crawlers' Favor, and somebody is selling.
Story: Nobody in Denver has met him. Everybody in Denver has heard the terms: real gold, up front, for a permanent share of your audience attention, System-witnessed and irreversible. Several parties are known to have signed. Nobody knows what he is doing with the accumulated Favor, and nobody has thought carefully about what a man with no audience of his own would want it for.
MechanicalHook: Offstage economic threat. His buyers can appear as NPCs long before he does. A late escalation, not an early one.

Name: AdaKettleworth
Deal: There is a room three floors down where nobody is allowed to fight, and she enforces it.
Story: Fed a congregation on Sunday and anyone who turned up the rest of the week, for thirty-one years. She has apparently done the same thing here, in a room the System has not managed to monetise. The rule is the rule: you eat, you leave your weapons at the door, and you do not bring it inside. Two parties who tested this are said to have left considerably worse off than the people they came for.
MechanicalHook: Neutral ground the party badly needs and cannot exploit. Whatever enforces her rule should never be shown directly.
Sponsor: (none, and the System has stopped asking)

Name: DamienOrtizHalliwell
Deal: He went down on day one, alone, and has never been announced dead.
Story: Summited things without ropes and dived systems nobody had mapped, and walked into the Denver entry point eleven hours after the Collapse with a headlamp and no plan at all. The System announces every death. It has not announced his. Depending on who is telling it, that means he is the deepest living human being on Earth, or it means he found the thing at the bottom and it has better uses for him.
MechanicalHook: The party's eventual proof that the floors do not end. Best kept as a name on a wall, scratched deeper than anyone should have been able to reach.

Name: TheGardener
Deal: Somebody is planting things in the dungeon, and some of them are coming up.
Story: Pockets of growing matter keep appearing in rooms with no light and no soil - arranged, deliberate, and in at least two cases edible. The System has classified them as an unlicensed environmental modification and is charging a fee it has nobody to bill. Whoever is doing it moves ahead of the parties and has never been seen.
MechanicalHook: Ambient hope. Small free heals in unexpected places. Reveal only if it is worth more revealed than not, which it probably is not.

Name: ColetteNwachukwuBarr
Deal: She only kills crawlers who have signed sponsorship deals, and she has never once been wrong about who has.
Story: Spent a career suing companies for what they put inside people. Down here she has decided that the sponsorship contract is the actual crime and the signatories are the actual accomplices, which is either a coherent moral position or six floors of rationalisation. Her Favor is enormous. The audience adores a heel with a thesis.
MechanicalHook: A direct threat the moment the party takes their first sponsor. Turns accepting a deal into a real decision instead of free money.
Sponsor: (kills for it; will not take one)

Name: TheFourFifteen
Deal: Something arrives in the same room every day at 4:15 AM local time, and local time is a thing the System keeps mentioning.
Story: The floor-open announcement always gives the local time, and it is always wrong except once a day. Crawlers who have been down long enough have noticed that at 4:15 AM, whatever room they happen to be in, something is briefly present and then is not. Nobody has been hurt by it. That is somehow worse.
MechanicalHook: A recurring timed beat that costs nothing to run. Never explain it. The moment it becomes a mechanic it stops being the best thing in the bar.

Name: WendellAmagiSoto
Deal: He mapped two entire floors correctly and the map is still down there somewhere.
Story: Thirty years surveying the Front Range, and he applied every bit of it: proper triangulation, elevation profiles, a legend. He finished Floor 2 and was most of the way through Floor 3 when a Debt Eater found him. The map is real, it is accurate, and it is in a bag in a room nobody has identified. Four parties are actively looking.
MechanicalHook: A treasure hunt whose payoff is information, not gear. Whoever finds it gets the floor layout - worth more than any weapon, and far easier to author.

Name: GraceOyelaranPike
Deal: Held a doorway for ninety seconds so eleven strangers could get through it.
Story: Nobody in that stairwell knew her name; they had it off the death announcement, which the System delivered in the same tone it uses for patch notes. Eleven people are alive on Floor 2 because of ninety seconds of work by someone who was not strong, was not armed, and was nobody's idea of a hero. Her name is now scratched into the wall of that stairwell fourteen separate times, in fourteen different hands.
MechanicalHook: The graffiti is the content. Put her name on that wall and let players find it without a quest marker.

Name: TobiasReinholtCruz
Deal: Calculated the survival odds correctly, announced them, and was killed by the resulting stampede.
Story: He was right. That is the whole joke, and the System has never let it go - his numbers were accurate to within two percent, and the panic they caused killed forty people including him. The achievement named after him is awarded to any crawler who shares genuinely bad news with a group.
MechanicalHook: An achievement with a person behind it. Ties the existing achievement system to a name instead of a pun.

Name: IngridSolbergAdeyemi
Deal: Held the fastest floor clear in Denver for six days and died eleven metres from the exit.
Story: Ran a hundred miles at a time for fun, and treated the dungeon as terrain, which worked extremely well right up until it did not. Her time still tops the Denver leaderboard. The System has left it there, because an unbeaten record set by a dead woman is better engagement than a living champion, and it says so openly.
MechanicalHook: Her time is the number on the leaderboard the party is chasing. Beating it should feel bad.

Name: MarcusKettlebyOsei
Deal: Got sixty-one children down two floors and did not get down the third.
Story: Every account agrees on the count and none of them agree on how. He was not a fighter and had no skills worth listing. What he had was thirty years of moving large numbers of frightened young people through a building calmly, and it turns out that is a skill the dungeon had no answer for, until it simply outlasted him.
MechanicalHook: The reason there are children in the Floor 3 safe rooms. Do not show the death; show the sixty-one.

Name: LenaVasquezHolt
Deal: Turned down four sponsorship offers, and the fifth thing that found her was not an offer.
Story: Nineteen, first year, and stubborn in the specific way that only works if you live through it. She refused every deal on the grounds that she had not agreed to be in a show and was not going to start now, which the audience found charming and then irritating. Her Favor bottomed out. Favor is what the System spends on soft spawns.
MechanicalHook: The cautionary tale the bar tells about refusing sponsorship - deliberately in tension with Colette Nwachukwu-Barr, who kills people for accepting.

Name: HaroldMbekiStrand
FormerLife: Retired; drank in the same bar since 1979
Deal: Died in his usual seat, in a bar that had been dragged underground with him still in it.
Story: The Collapse took every roofed structure on Earth in the same instant, and a great many people were indoors. Harold was on his stool. Whatever the dungeon did to that building, it kept the bar and it kept him, and he stayed there eleven days being served by staff who were also not okay, and then he stopped. Nobody moved him for a while. It did not seem right.
MechanicalHook: Sets the Bar's tone in one beat: the staff are not fine, and the regulars were here first.

Name: SamiraDoyleFontaine
Deal: Found an exploit that trivialised a boss, and was patched out along with it.
Story: Twelve years of breaking software professionally, and she broke the Voldemortgage encounter inside forty minutes - a genuine, reproducible sequence break. She wrote it up. She shared it. Four parties used it. Then came a balance patch, delivered with the System's usual warmth, and the patch notes listed her by name under 'Fixed'.
MechanicalHook: The party can still find her writeup. Any exploit they discover now carries the implication that using it puts them in the next patch notes.

Name: OmarBellingerKhan
Deal: Signed up on day two because the alternative was the surface, and lasted nine hours.
Story: The four million are volunteers, which is the distinction the System leans on whenever anyone objects to any of this. Omar volunteered. He had seen what was left up there and did the arithmetic in about a minute, and the arithmetic was correct - the show is the better option, which is the actual horror and not the monsters. Nine hours. The announcement gave his name, his sponsor status, and the local time.
MechanicalHook: Use his name in the intake announcement. He is what 'volunteer' means, said plainly, exactly once, with no joke attached.
